headline: Jack Kirby and Stan Lee: The Untold History
post:
Hey everyone! For decades, Stan Lee was the famous face of Marvel Comics, but things behind the scenes were a bit complicated. According to Screen Rant, a longtime grievance centered on how credit and creators' rights were handled for legendary heroes like The Avengers and the X-Men. Jack Kirby, who co-created iconic characters alongside Lee, often felt his overall writing and plotting contributions were minimized while the publisher received the spotlight. 

Their working relationship dates all the way back to the 1940s at Timely Comics. Later, the famous "Marvel Method" became the standard workflow, where artists handled the bulk of the storytelling and plotting while Lee wrote the dialogue. Tensions grew as Lee became the public face of the company, leading Kirby to voice his frustrations in later interviews and even satire. 

Disputes over original artwork and copyright claims continued for years, sparking important conversations about creators' rights in the comic industry. Did you know about the history behind these classic superhero creations? 📚✨

#MarvelHistory #JackKirby #StanLee
original_title: Why The Avengers' Co-Creator Ended Up Hating Stan Lee

headline: Christopher Yates brings Night Vision to Tallinn
post:
Writer-director Christopher Yates has unveiled his self-produced fiction feature debut, according to The Hollywood Reporter. The movie follows a young filmmaker named Jenny who purchases an old video camera at a flea market, only to discover strange artifacts and presences on the tape. 

According to the publication, the project blends autofiction, found footage, romance, and horror while following dream logic. Yates created the animation and special effects himself using YouTube tutorials before securing finishing grants to pay professionals. The cast features Salomé Crickx, Pierre Gervais, and Angelo Bison.
